## Outdoor Holding Company Reports Second Quarter Fiscal 2027 Financial Results


November 16, 2026


*Revenue increased 14.6% to $13.7 million and net income from continuing operations increased to $2.3 million; first-half cash flow from continuing operations improved by $16.4 million from the prior-year period*


**Dallas, Texas, Nov. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) --** Outdoor Holding Company (Nasdaq: POWW, POWWP) (“OHC,” “we,” “us,” “our” or the “Company”), the owner of[GunBroker.com](http://gunbroker.com/) , the largest online marketplace dedicated to firearms, hunting, shooting and related products, today reported its financial results for its fiscal second quarter ended September 30, 2026.


**Second Quarter Fiscal 2027 vs. Second Quarter Fiscal 2026**


- Revenue growth continued: net revenues increased 14.6% to $13.7 million from $12.0 million, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of year-over-year growth
- Cost of revenues, exclusive of depreciation and amortization, was 15.4% of net revenues compared to 12.9% in the prior-year period, reflecting the per-transaction cost of Federal Firearms License (“FFL”) transfer services and higher transaction volume
- Depreciation and amortization expense, including platform software amortization, was $3.8 million, compared with $3.6 million
- Total costs and expenses increased 3.7% to $11.7 million from $11.3 million; income from operations increased to $2.0 million from $0.7 million
- Net income from continuing operations increased approximately 63.6% to $2.3 million from $1.4 million; net income margin was 16.7%, compared with 11.7%
- Net income attributable to common shareholders increased to $1.5 million, or $0.01 per basic and diluted share, from $0.7 million, or $0.01 per basic and diluted share, in the prior-year period
- Adjusted EBITDA1 increased 24.7% to $6.1 million compared to $4.9 million in the same period last year
- Grew gross merchandise value (“GMV”) 10.3% year-over-year to approximately $208.4 million from approximately $189.0 million in the prior-year period
- **First-half results(compared to prior year period):** for the six months ended September 30, 2026, net revenues increased 18.3% to $28.2 million, net income from continuing operations was $5.9 million compared with a net loss from continuing operations of $(4.5) million, Adjusted EBITDA increased 74.3% to $14.0 million, and net cash provided by operating activities was $13.0 million, compared with net cash used in operating activities of $(3.5) million in the prior-year period, an improvement of $16.4 million


**Operational Highlights**


- Generated positive net income in four of the last five quarters
- Outperformed the broader firearms market as firearm unit sales increased 4.8%, compared with a 2.5% increase in adjusted FBI-managed National Instant Criminal Background Check System (“NICS checks”), increasing the Company’s estimated share of adjusted NICS activity by 16 basis points to approximately 6.3%; for the first six months of fiscal 2027, firearm unit sales increased 8.1% compared with a 3.9% increase in adjusted NICS checks, and the Company’s estimated share increased 29 basis points to approximately 6.4%
- Increased take rate 25 basis points year over year to 6.59%; Federal Firearms License (“FFL”) transfer revenue contributed 40 basis points, demonstrating the opportunity to expand transaction monetization without increasing the base final value fee
- Total items sold increased 1.9% to 429,777; grew average order value 8.3% year-over-year to $485 and firearm GMV by 11.3%, with new and used firearms each up more than 11%; GMV in the silencers and suppressed firearms category more than doubled year-over-year to approximately $3.0 million
- Repurchased 2,442,022 shares of common stock during the quarter for $5.4 million at an average price of $2.20 per share excluding commissions and fees; subsequent to quarter end, the Board of Directors increased the repurchase authorization by $20.0 million and extended the program to July 4, 2027, leaving $24.5 million available immediately following the amendment
- Grew cash and cash equivalents to $70.4 million, an increase of $1.6 million during the quarter, despite funding $5.4 million of share repurchases and $0.8 million of preferred stock dividends
- Completed the Company’s redomestication from Delaware to Texas effective September 30, 2026


“Our second-quarter results demonstrate the strength of GunBroker's marketplace model and the progress we're making in executing our strategy,” said Steve Urvan, Chairman and CEO of Outdoor Holding Company. “Despite the normal seasonal softness of the July to September quarter, revenue grew nearly 15%, income from operations nearly tripled, and Adjusted EBITDA expanded. We also continued gaining market share, increased our take rate through value-added services rather than higher base fees, and generated sufficient cash to fund substantial share repurchases while increasing our cash balance.”


“Our operating philosophy is simple: **Continuous Improvement. Disciplined Growth.** We believe operational improvement is never finished. We will continue simplifying the business, improving efficiency, and allocating capital to its highest and best use. At the same time, we're investing selectively in initiatives that strengthen the marketplace, improve the customer experience, and expand the revenue we earn from each transaction. Our objective is not simply to reduce costs or grow revenue, but to build a business that consistently generates attractive returns and creates long-term shareholder value.”


Second-quarter net revenues increased 14.6% to $13.7 million, including approximately $0.8 million of FFL transfer revenue. Final-value fees and optional listing feature revenue increased 9.3% to $8.5 million from $7.7 million. Total costs and expenses increased $0.4 million, or 3.7%, to $11.7 million. Corporate general and administrative expenses increased $0.4 million to $3.2 million, reflecting the redomestication costs and higher legal expense, partially offset by the prior-year Vista settlement expense. Employee salaries and related expenses decreased $0.7 million to $2.6 million, reflecting lower headcount and severance costs, partially offset by stock-based compensation. Approximately $0.5 million of redomestication expense and $0.4 million of AI-related expense remained included in Adjusted EBITDA. Income from operations increased to $2.0 million from $0.7 million.


Cost of revenues, excluding depreciation and amortization, increased $0.6 million to $2.1 million from $1.5 million, reflecting FFL service costs and higher transaction volume. Depreciation and amortization increased $0.2 million to $3.8 million from $3.6 million, reflecting continued investment in capitalized platform development. See “Change in Presentation” below for a discussion regarding a change in presentation of the Company’s condensed consolidated statements of operations.


For the first six months of fiscal 2027, net revenues increased 18.3% to $28.2 million and GMV increased 14.2% to $432.2 million. Total costs and expenses declined 21.5% to $22.9 million from $29.1 million. Income from operations was $5.3 million, compared with a loss from operations of $5.3 million in the prior-year period. Net income from continuing operations was $5.9 million, compared with a net loss of $4.5 million. Net income attributable to common shareholders was $4.3 million, or $0.04 per basic share and $0.03 per diluted share, compared with a loss of $6.6 million, or $0.06 per basic and diluted share. Adjusted EBITDA increased 74.3% to $14.0 million from $8.0 million.


[GunBroker.com](http://gunbroker.com/) delivered solid marketplace performance during the second fiscal quarter, with GMV, firearm units, average order value and take rate all increasing year-over-year against a prior-year quarter that had no legislation-driven demand, reflecting continued engagement from both buyers and sellers and the effect of recent platform investments.


● Firearm unit sales increased 4.8% year-over-year, outpacing the 2.5% increase in adjusted NICS checks and reflecting a 16 basis point increase in the Company’s share of adjusted NICS checks, to approximately 6.3%; for the first six months of fiscal 2027, firearm unit sales increased 8.1% compared with a 3.9% increase in adjusted NICS checks, and the Company’s share increased 29 basis points to approximately 6.4%


● Total GMV increased 10.3% year-over-year to approximately $208.4 million; firearm GMV increased 11.3%, with new and used firearms each up more than 11%


● Take rate (net revenues divided by GMV) increased 25 basis points year-over-year to 6.59%, driven primarily by FFL transfer revenue, which contributed 40 basis points; excluding FFL transfer revenue, take rate was modestly lower, reflecting mix toward firearms and the Company’s largest sellers


● Average order value grew 8.3% year-over-year to $485, and firearm average order value grew 6.2% to $872


During the quarter, the Company continued to introduce platform enhancements designed to improve marketplace efficiency and user experience. In its second full quarter of operation, the Company’s FFL transfer integration continued to deliver centralized dealer verification and a streamlined transfer workflow, while contributing FFL transfer revenue of $0.8 million and 40 basis points of take rate on approximately 200,000 transfers. FFL transfer services carry a per-transaction cost and therefore retain a smaller share of revenue than the Company’s legacy marketplace fees, but management does not view this mix shift as a deterioration in the underlying economics of the business. New transaction-related services are expected to generate attractive incremental revenue and expand take rate by monetizing additional portions of the transaction without requiring an increase in the base final value fee. Excluding FFL transfer revenue, take rate was modestly lower than in the prior-year quarter, primarily reflecting mix toward firearms and the Company’s largest sellers, which carry lower fee rates. Excluding FFL transfer revenue, net revenues grew approximately 8%.


The Company continues to implement AI where management believes it can produce measurable improvements in marketplace productivity and user experience. The AI-powered listing tool launched in March continued to standardize product descriptions across the marketplace and improve searchability, and the Company continues to enhance it. The Company’s AI-supported customer-service agent is now in production, which is intended to resolve routine inquiries before a support ticket is created, with human escalation preserved for complex matters, and is being extended to additional high-volume support workflows. The Company incurred approximately $0.4 million of AI-related costs during the quarter, which were largely one-time in nature, and expects to continue investing in AI where the return is measurable. The benefits depend on successful deployment, data quality, adoption, system reliability and ongoing technology costs, and may require additional development expenditures and operating expenses.


Universal payment processing remains a priority. Nearly 30% of marketplace transactions are not paid by card today, and card checkout for those transactions is the largest remaining source of friction in the buying process. Additional initiatives are being evaluated to improve listing efficiency, reduce customer-service response times and lower transaction friction. The Company continues to work through the compliance requirements associated with the initiative and is evaluating commercial arrangements with payment providers, technical integration, underwriting and compliance requirements, and the availability of payment services for firearms-related commerce. Delays, higher processing or compliance costs, unfavorable terms or lower adoption could defer or reduce expected benefits, although management believes that, if implemented, such an initiative could reduce transaction friction and increase conversion.


The second quarter is seasonally the softest period of the Company’s fiscal year. The quarter nevertheless marked the first year-over-year increase in second quarter GMV since fiscal 2021. Within the quarter, adjusted NICS checks decelerated from an 8.5% year-over-year increase in July to a 2.3% year-over-year decrease in September, while the Company’s FFL-required unit sales grew between 4% and 7% year-over-year in each month. Trailing-twelve-month active buyers increased 2.6% year-over-year to approximately 410,000, and GMV per active seller increased 12.1%. Active sellers were approximately 36,000, down 1.6% year-over-year. Registered users exceeded 9.0 million at the end of the quarter.


**Change in Presentation**


Beginning with the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the Company changed the presentation of its condensed consolidated statements of operations. All costs are now presented in a single “costs and expenses” section. Cost of revenues is presented exclusive of depreciation and amortization, and all depreciation and amortization — including amortization of capitalized platform development costs — is presented as a separate line item. Because depreciation and amortization is excluded from cost of revenues, and consistent with SEC staff guidance for that presentation, the Company no longer presents a gross profit subtotal, and no longer presents a total operating expenses subtotal. Prior-period amounts have been conformed to the new presentation. The change does not affect any previously reported amount, including net revenues, income (loss) from operations, net income (loss), income (loss) per share, cash flows, the balance sheet or shareholders’ equity. Amortization of capitalized platform development costs continues to be reported in depreciation and amortization, and Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes all depreciation and amortization, is unaffected. As a result of the change, the Company discusses margin in terms of cost of revenues as a percentage of net revenues rather than gross margin. Cost of revenues, exclusive of depreciation and amortization, was 15.4% of net revenues for the quarter, compared with 12.9% in the prior-year quarter, and 15.4% for the first six months of fiscal 2027 compared with 12.9% in the prior-year period. The year-over-year increase reflects the per-transaction cost of FFL transfer services and higher transaction volume.


**Balance Sheet and Liquidity**


The Company ended the quarter with $70.4 million in cash and cash equivalents, an increase of $1.6 million during the quarter and $2.3 million from March 31, 2026. Net cash provided by operating activities was $13.0 million for the six months ended September 30, 2026, compared with net cash used in operating activities of $3.5 million in the prior-year period, an improvement of $16.4 million. Operating cash flow for the second quarter was approximately $8.5 million, compared with approximately $3.2 million in the prior-year quarter, and included receipt of a $2.0 million reimbursement under the Company’s D&O insurance policy for costs related to the previously disclosed SEC Investigation. The Company grew its cash balance despite funding $7.4 million of share repurchases under its share repurchase program, $1.4 million of preferred stock dividends, and a $0.2 million principal payment and $0.8 million of interest on the related-party note during the first six months of the fiscal year. The Company has no bank debt. Its revolving credit facility, which had no outstanding balance, was terminated effective April 1, 2026. The strengthened balance sheet and liquidity position provide significant flexibility to support ongoing platform investments, pursue selective strategic opportunities, and return value to shareholders through the share repurchase program. With no bank debt, lower fixed costs, and more consistent profitability, the Company is well-positioned to fund organic growth initiatives while maintaining a disciplined approach to capital allocation and shareholder value creation.


During the quarter, the Company repurchased 2,442,022 shares of common stock for $5.4 million at an average price of $2.20 per share, excluding commissions and fees. Since the program’s launch in January 2026, the Company has repurchased 3,975,951 shares at an average price of $2.11 per share, and $6.6 million remained available under the original $15.0 million authorization at September 30, 2026. On October 19, 2026, the Board of Directors increased the aggregate repurchase authorization by $20.0 million, to $35.0 million (inclusive of all repurchases since the program’s inception), and extended the program by six months, to July 4, 2027. Immediately following the amendment, $24.5 million remained available for repurchases. Repurchases may be made from time to time through open market purchases, privately negotiated transactions and other means in accordance with federal securities laws, including pursuant to Rule 10b5-1 trading plans. The program does not obligate the Company to repurchase any specific number of shares and may be modified, suspended or terminated at any time.


**Corporate Developments**


Effective September 30, 2026, the Company completed its redomestication from Delaware to Texas by conversion pursuant to a plan of conversion approved by the Board of Directors and shareholders, and adopted a Certificate of Formation and Bylaws governed by the Texas Business Organizations Code. The Company’s principal executive offices are now located in Dallas, Texas. Separately, in July 2026 the Company delivered a certification and supporting documentation to the SEC Staff that, in the Company’s opinion, it had fully complied with the undertakings concerning the remediation of material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting required by the SEC’s December 2025 cease-and-desist order. In October 2026, the SEC Staff indicated that they had reviewed the Company’s certification and supporting documentation and had no further questions or follow-up regarding the Company’s submission. The Company continues to maintain and monitor its internal controls. The Company expects to continue incurring settlement-compliance and indemnification costs, which may be material in individual reporting periods.


**Fiscal 2027 Execution Priorities**


The Company’s strategy is focused on four execution priorities for the remainder of fiscal 2027:


1. Growing marketplace activity and market share through improvements in buyer engagement, seller participation and transaction velocity;
2. Expanding transaction monetization by scaling FFL transfer revenue and implementing universal payments;
3. Protecting the reset cost structure through disciplined hiring, vendor management and return-based investment, while reinvesting in technology, seller growth and customer service where returns are measurable; and
4. Deploying AI where it can produce measurable improvements in listing quality, customer-service efficiency and transaction friction.


Management believes these initiatives can increase revenue earned from each transaction, capture incremental market share and support durable profitability without increasing the base final value fee.


**Discontinued Operations**


As previously disclosed, in April 2025, the Company completed the sale of all assets of its business of designing, manufacturing, marketing, distributing and selling ammunition and ammunition components, along with certain related assets and liabilities (the “Transaction”), which previously comprised the Company’s Ammunition segment. Following the Transaction, the Company continues to operate its online e-commerce marketplace business[GunBroker.com](http://gunbroker.com/) .


For the purposes of this earnings release and the financial information provided herein, the results of the Company’s former Ammunition segment are presented as discontinued operations in the consolidated statements of operations for all periods presented, if applicable.

**About Outdoor Holding Company**


Outdoor Holding Company is the publicly traded parent and operator of GunBroker.com, the largest online marketplace dedicated to firearms, hunting, shooting and related products. Third-party sellers list items on the site and federal and state laws govern the sale of firearms and other restricted items. Firearms sold through the marketplace are transferred through federally licensed firearms dealers in accordance with applicable law. Launched in 1999, the[GunBroker.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=_yRc5Ja4cF7iJre8OiOEM-JdPytfn_aPP8hiez1bFrzYChiahtKqcQiMi05tNoM0zVABhhqji1SLZe-sUWJZDstGVLZQWJxzx7OYztiBDx4=) website is an informative, secure and safe way to buy and sell firearms, ammunition, shooting accessories and outdoor gear online. GunBroker promotes responsible ownership of guns and firearms. We have included these non-GAAP financial measures in this press release because they are key measures management uses to evaluate our operational performance, produce future strategies for our operations, and make strategic decisions, including those relating to operating expenses and the allocation of our resources. Accordingly, we believe that these measures provide useful information to investors and others in understanding and evaluating our operating results in the same manner as our management and Board of Directors. Adjusted EBITDA is a non-GAAP financial measure that displays our net income (loss) from continuing operations (the most directly comparable financial measure prepared in accordance with GAAP), adjusted to eliminate the effect of certain items described below. We define Adjusted EBITDA as net income (loss) from continuing operations excluding (i) provision or benefit for income taxes, (ii) depreciation and amortization, (iii) interest expense, net, (iv) stock-based compensation expenses relating to stock awards and common stock purchase options, (v) interest and other income (expense), net, (vi) expenses related to acquisitions and divestitures, (vii) gain on extinguishment of debt, (viii) professional service and legal fees related to an investigation conducted by a special committee of the Board of Directors (the “Special Committee Investigation”), an investigation by the SEC (“the SEC Investigation”) and the now-settled lawsuit related to the GunBroker acquisition (the “Delaware Litigation”) (ix) other nonrecurring expenses, such as contingencies associated with litigation or settlements and (x) corporate restructuring costs related to headcount reductions, severance, and expense consolidation.


We believe that it is useful to exclude these items because the amount of such items in any specific period may not directly correlate to the underlying performance of our business operations. Non-GAAP financial measures have limitations, should be considered as supplemental in nature and are not meant as a substitute for the related financial information prepared in accordance with GAAP. These limitations include the following:


- stock-based compensation expense has been, and will continue to be for the foreseeable future, a significant recurring expense for the Company and an important part of our compensation strategy;

- non-GAAP measures do not reflect changes in, or cash requirements for, our working capital needs; and
- other companies, including companies in our industry, may calculate their non-GAAP financial measures differently or not at all, which reduces their usefulness as comparative measures.


Because of these limitations, you should consider the non-GAAP financial measures alongside other financial performance measures, including our net income (loss) from continuing operations and our other financial results presented in accordance with GAAP.
